articles.title: Savannah Guthrie Shares New Post Asking for Information About Her Mother’s Disappearance: ‘We Ache for Her, We Cry Out for Answers’
articles.summary: Savannah Guthrie has taken to social media to urge anyone with knowledge about her mother, Nancy, who was presumed kidnapped in February and has yet to be found, to come forward.
body: “The world goes on, things appear ‘normal’ – as we try to keep going and be strong, especially for our young kids – but it’s not and it never will be,” Guthrie’s caption continued. “For Annie and Tommy, for Cam and Kristine, for Mike and me and for all of mom’s beloved grandchildren: we ache for her, we cry out for answers, we cannot move forward. We need someone to help us, tell us what you know. Our mom was a light in this world. We want to celebrate her and give her the dignity she deserves. The reward is still available. Please. We are begging you. Please help us.”
She concluded: “Thank you to all those who have been kind and shown the best of humanity. Join us in praying without ceasing.”

In August, Guthrie shared a post to commemorate 6 months since her mother was kidnapped. “We have lived every moment, every breath, and every heartbeat in agony and despair ever since,” she wrote. “Every day, we wake up and try to be strong and go on — because that’s what our joyful and resilient Mom taught us to do.”

articles.title: Harry Styles Closes Out 30-Night Madison Square Garden Residency With Two ‘Harryween’ Shows, Dressed as Elvis and Pizza Rat, and a Jalen Brunson Guest Appearance
articles.summary: Harry Styles record-setting 30-night residency at New York’s Madison Square Garden came to a close over the weekend, with a pair of Styles’ recurring “Harryween” concerts that saw the star, his band and much of the audience dressed for the occasion — in his case as 1970s-era Elvis Presley on the…
body: The themed costumes were not limited to the singer: On Friday, Styles’ band was dressed in his own iconic looks, rocking outfits based on his Coachella, Met Gala and Grammy appearances. “The theme on stage tonight was favorite sequined king,” he joked, later thanking the audience for considering him part of that group. For the encore, the arena was taken back in time as he emerged in his 2010 “X-Factor” audition outfit, singing Stevie Wonder’s “Isn’t She Lovely.” His version of the song was what clinched the then-bakery-worker a spot in One Direction over 15 years ago.

The final show on Saturday was, in its entirety, a tribute to New York City. The band took the stage first, all dressed as local icons including the Statue of Liberty, Andy Warhol and Anna Wintour, before Styles himself appeared as “Pizza Rat,” based on a notorious 2015 meme showing a large rat dragging a slice of pizza down the stairs of a New York City subway station. In another nod to the city, this time in the form of music history, the pop star delivered a compelling cover of Talking Heads’ “Psycho Killer” before reverting to the standard setlist.

articles.title: Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything’ and ‘Clayface’ Battle for No. 1 With $10.5 Million in Sleepy Halloween Weekend
articles.summary: A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” and DC’s comic book adaptation “Clayface” are vying for first place at the domestic box office, with each film on track to collect around $10.5 million over the weekend.
body: “That’s a rare achievement for any film, let alone a documentary running more than three hours,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian.

Overall, it was another painfully slow Halloween for cinema owners without any new releases, as well as the misfortune of the holiday landing on Saturday. When Halloween coincides with the weekend, families prefer to go trick-or-treating rather than visit their local multiplex. Revenues between Friday and Sunday amounted to roughly $62 million to $64 million, marking one of the slowest weekends of the year, according to Rentrak. However, it’s an improvement from 2025’s Halloween weekend, which resulted in $49 million across all films, led by Colleen Hoover adaptation “Regretting You” and “Black Phone 2.”
“With costume parties, trick-or-treating and countless other Halloween activities, theaters were facing some pretty stiff competition for people’s time and attention,” Dergarabedian says.

articles.title: Michael Mann Hospitalized After Accidentally Shooting Himself in the Leg at Los Angeles Gun Range
articles.summary: Michael Mann was hospitalized on Saturday after he accidentally shot himself in the leg at a Los Angeles gun range, according to the L.A. Police Department. The director was trying to holster a firearm during a target practice at a sanctioned gun range when the weapon accidentally went off, as…
body: “On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann. He was treated and is being released,” Mann’s reps said in a statement.

Mann is best known for directing such movies as “Heat,” “Thief,” “Manhunter,” “Miami Vice” and “The Insider.” He last directed 2023’s “Ferrari,” a sports biopic starring Adam Driver as Enzo Ferrari and Penelope Cruz as his wife Laura.

The 83-year-old filmmaker is currently working on “Heat 2,” the long-awaited sequel to his 1995 crime drama starring Al Pacino and Robert De Niro. The first film, a box office hit, follows an explosive face-off between Los Angeles Police Department detective Lieutenant Vincent Hanna (Pacino) and professional thief Neil McCauley (De Niro). Mann adapted the screenplay for “Heat 2” from the 2022 novel of the same name that he co-wrote with Meg Gardiner. Described as a sequel and prequel to the original, the follow-up looks at the early lives of Pacino and De Niro’s characters. The cast is expected to include Leonardo DiCaprio, Christian Bale and Adam Driver.

articles.title: Gavin and Stacey actor hopes his band will be 'the next Stereophonics'
articles.summary: Oscar Hartland, who played Neil the Baby, says he's on a "mission to create a new modern sound for Wales".
body: Gavin and Stacey fans will likely remember Oscar Hartland, or Neil the Baby, for his heart-warming performance of The Beatle's Blackbird in the sitcom's 2024 finale.
The episode was watched by about 12.3m people on Christmas day and saw Hartland's character serenade the crowd at the wedding of his on-screen dad Smithy, played by James Cordon.
But that was just the start for Hartland, now 17, who says his band is aiming to be "the next 'Phonics, or something like that".
Hartland, from Machen, Caerphilly county, said his latest release, Wild Bull, was rooted in "being a bit crazy" and the challenges of growing up in the south Wales valleys.

articles.title: Romeo + Juliet at 30: how Baz Luhrmann made teens fall in love with Shakespeare
articles.summary: The maximalist, heart over head adaptation of the romantic tragedy made stars of its leads and became an English teacher’s most trusted weapon for Bard-averse students. Romeo + Juliet is not the most renowned or beloved of Shakespeare’s plays, but it is perhaps the most foundational.
body: As such, the blatantly youth-aimed film had plenty of detractors in its time. Critics dismissed it as vulgar and garish, but audiences turned out en masse; Romeo + Juliet made over $147m against a $14.5m budget, boosted in part by a period-defining soundtrack with needle drops from The Cardigans, Everclear, Radiohead and Garbage. (And of course, the song from that oft-replayed fish tank scene, Des’ree’s I’m Kissing You, became the ubiquitous soundtrack for couple-shipping montage videos on 2000s YouTube). By the time I first viewed the film in 2009 – like many, in high school English class, as part of my teacher’s bid to get us invested in Shakespeare – it was already considered a classic.

articles.title: Sir Tom Jones mentors Welsh singer to victory on The Voice UK
articles.summary: Cate McHugh was congratulated by her coach Sir Tom Jones after she was crowned winner on Saturday.
body: A singer who began her career as a teenager busking on the streets of Cardiff has been crowned winner of The Voice UK.
Cate McHugh, from Llantwit Major in the Vale of Glamorgan, appeared stunned when she heard her name announced on the ITV show, telling viewers "I did it" when asked how she was feeling.

The performer, who has a degenerative sight condition which has left her registered blind, was given a congratulatory hug by her coach Sir Tom Jones on his final appearance on the show after previously announcing he had been "fired".
Speaking after the show, McHugh, 31, said: "I won The Voice! I'm entirely gobsmacked and absolutely haven't fully processed this information just yet."

articles.title: ‘You Can See Everything,’ ‘Clayface’ Fighting for No. 1 in Quiet Halloween Weekend
articles.summary: The Elizabeth Holmes documentary could land the first No. 1 of its buzzy three-week run as the studios avoided major releases over the spooky frame.
body: A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything, which includes a memorable discussion about the classic comedy routine “Who’s on First,” sparked questions about whether the movie itself could take first place over Clayface as the two films battled during a subdued Halloween weekend.

Just behind it for the time being is Clayface, as filmmaker James Watkins’ body horror feature looks to gross around $10.4 million in its sophomore frame for a two-week North American sum of $44.1 million. Tom Rhys Harries and Naomi Ackie star in the $44 million-budgeted Warner Bros. release that marks DC Studios ‘ third theatrical title for bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran after 2025’s Superman and this summer’s underperforming Supergirl. Clayface looks to decline around 56 percent for the weekend.

Overall, this weekend is headed for one of the lowest domestic totals of the year and may come in at just above the $49 million collected over the equivalent weekend in 2025. Last year, Halloween fell on Friday as Black Phone 2 led the frame with $8.3 million in its third weekend.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart Had A Surprising Love For This Classic MTV Animated Series
articles.summary: The great Patrick Stewart may have become most famous for playing serious authority figures, but his personal taste occasionally leaned in crude directions.
body: The late, great Sir Patrick Stewart had a silly streak you might not know about. Case in point: He was a big, big fan of Mike Judge's MTV animated series "Beavis and Butt-Head," the perennial Gen-X text about two snickering teenage wastoids who do little other than make butt jokes. In a 2020 interview with National Post, Stewart called the series "brilliant."

The actor landed in the population's mass consciousness when he began playing the stern authority figure of Captain Jean-Luc Picard on "Star Trek: The Next Generation" in 1987. Film fans might also have recognized him from earlier films like John Boorman's "Excalibur," David Lynch's "Dune," or Tobe Hooper's "Lifeforce," and he played very serious characters in those films as well. Stewart was an authoritative, stalwart presence in most of his roles.

articles.title: 15 Best Western Movies Of The 2020s (So Far)
articles.summary: The Western genre may not be thriving in the way it did during Hollywood's Golden Age, but there have been some excellent Westerns produced in the 2020s.
body: The Western may be the prototypical American film genre, but it's long past its glory days. While Hollywood's Golden Age saw Westerns produced at an exponential rate compared to other genres, it has been on the defensive since the old studio system's collapse and the arrival of New Hollywood auteurs in the '70s. America was ready to move on from the old-fashioned forms of mythology it had been fed for decades.

However, the Western has never truly died. Every decade since then has seen attempts to spin the genre anew, many of which stand out as essential modern entries. We already have a list of the 15 best Western movies of the 21st century, but we want to take a look at our current decade so far. The year 2020 has, admittedly, been a light stretch for the genre, but we still have a worthy list of movies that embrace Hollywood's most established genre conventions or, more often than not, subvert them to communicate something new.

articles.title: Michael Mann Accidentally Shoots Himself at L.A. Gun Range
articles.summary: The incident happened on Saturday during target practice at a sanctioned gun range.
body: Michael Mann was hospitalized on Saturday after accidentally shooting himself at a gun range in Los Angeles, The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

“On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann. He was treated and is being released,” a rep for the four-time Oscar-nominated filmmaker shared in a statement.

Mann is currently in pre-production on Heat 2, which reportedly has Leonardo DiCaprio, Stephen Graham and Christian Bale attached to star. The film comes more than three decades after the 1995 crime drama Heat that starred Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Val Kilmer and Jon Voight.

He’s also best known for directing 1981’s Thief, 1999’s The Insider, 2001’s Ali, 2004’s Collateral, 2006’s Miami Vice, 2009’s Public Enemies and 2023’s Ferrari, among others. Throughout his career, he’s received four Academy Award nominations, including best director, best picture and best adapted screenplay for The Insider, and best picture for 2005’s The Aviator.
